}}'''Bernhard Örn Pálsson''' (born February 22, 1957 in [[Reykjavík]], Iceland<ref>{{cite news| url=https://timarit.is/page/6891154#page/n25/mode/2up |newspaper=[[Morgunblaðið]] |date=2017-02-22 |title=Frumkvöðull við rannsóknir i lífefnaverkræði |lang=is |trans-title=Pioneer in biochemical engineering research |page=26}}</ref>) is the Galletti [[Professor]] of [[Biomedical engineering|Bioengineering]] and an adjunct professor of [[Medicine]] at the [[University of California, San Diego]].<ref name="ucsd">http://gcrg.ucsd.edu/Researchers/Palsson {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720082237/http://gcrg.ucsd.edu/Researchers/Palsson |date=2011-07-20 }} Bernhard Palsson at USCD</ref><ref name=scopus>{{Scopus|id=8108272000}}</ref>

==Research==
Upon graduation Palsson joined the chemical engineering faculty at [[University of Michigan]] where he served as a professor until 1995. In 1995, he joined the department of Bioengineering at [[University of California, San Diego]] and was named the Galetti Chair of Bioengineering in 2004. In 2005 he became a faculty member of [[Keio University]].<ref name="biosustain" />

Palsson has authored or co-authored over 300 peer-reviewed scientific articles<ref>{{PubMedAuthorSearch|Palsson|BO}}</ref><ref>https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=bernhard+palsson Bernhard Palsson in [[Google Scholar]]</ref> and is the holder of over 35 patents.<ref name="ucsd"/> His research interests include [[metabolic network modelling]],<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Varma | first1 = A. | last2 = Palsson | first2 = B. Palsson serves on the editorial board of several scientific journals including ''Annals of Biomedical Engineering'', ''[[Biotechnology and Bioengineering]]'', ''[[Metabolic Engineering (journal)|Metabolic Engineering]]'' and ''[[Molecular Systems Biology]]''. He was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 2006 for scholarship, technological advances, and entrepreneurial activities in metabolic engineering. He is also a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 2011.
